what_this_sweep_established: Nineteen matrices in path order were written, layers 0 to 8 whole and layer 9's attention, where the sweeps before it wrote 2, 2 and 8. At every merge the engine itself read after a written matrix, 28 merges (the attention's merge, the feed-forward's merge and the layer's last merge of layers 0 to 8, and layer 9's attention), its own output holds every bound of the rows and of the means, the furthest part at 0.568 to 0.997 of its bound. No bound was drawn in and no matrix was chosen a second time.

With the mean and the rows held apart the pull has room at ten of the nineteen matrices. The tube loss left at each matrix's own merge, in path order: 0.629, 0.837, 0.658, 0.799, 0.871, 0.956, 0.971, 0.984, 0.911, 0.845, 0.691, 0.796, 0.710, 0.620, 0.633, 0.712, 0.746, 0.806, 0.838. Under the first allowance (controlled-bf16-3) every matrix after the first layer left 0.976 to 0.996. Beyond where their paths started, the matrices at positions 0, 1, 2, 3, 8, 9, 10, 12, 13 and 14 kept 0.371, 0.018, 0.306, 0.008, 0.075, 0.119, 0.160, 0.092, 0.191 and 0.027 of the tube loss at their own merges, each with every bound held on every third and on all the fitting answers together.

Through layer 7 a bringing back is cheap. Every matrix after the first arrived with a mean past its limit: at position 4 on one third only, at the others on all the fitting answers together, the furthest 2.1 to 30.8 times its limit at the matrix's own merge. A row part was past its limit at six of them (positions 2, 5, 8, 11, 17 and 18: one to three parts, at most 2.12 times). Positions 1 to 15 were brought back inside every bound of every third and of all together in 1 to 10 rounds and 9 to 221 s with 0.14% to 0.61% of the matrix changed, where the first allowance took 2.1% to 6.8%.

From layer 8 it is not. Layer 8's attention took 14 rounds and 1.04% of the matrix, the ridge stepped down to 2^-18 of the unit; layer 8's feed-forward, which arrived with 10 direction means and 25 size means past their limits (the furthest 28.5 times at its own merge and 33.6 at the layer's last) and one to three row parts, took 24 rounds, 561 s and 8.87% of the matrix with the ridge at its floor, 2^-23; layer 9's attention, with 31 size means past (9.2 times), took 16 rounds and 3.77% at 2^-19. All three ended inside every bound and were written. A bringing back gives back part of what arrives: layer 8's feed-forward arrived at 0.789 of its tube loss and was left at 0.806.

Where the pulls end. Of the eighteen paths after a bringing back, fifteen ended with every branch's read third past a bound and three with no solve taking a step (positions 11, 15 and 17: layers 5, 7 and 8's feed-forward). Nine matrices kept under 0.0001 of the tube loss beyond their bringing back: positions 4 to 7, 11 and 15 to 18.

where_it_ended.at: position 19, layer 9's feed-forward (6144 wide). It arrived at 0.861 of its tube loss with no row part outside and with 7 direction means and 20 size means past their limits at its own merge (the furthest 3.32 and 6.41 times) and 8 and 21 at the layer's last merge (3.33 and 8.54 times); 482.3 outside in all, a sum. The bringing back took that to 3.82, 0.537, 0.390, 0.315, 0.246 and 0.122 in six whole steps and went on with the ridge halved to its floor, 2^-23 of the unit: nineteen rounds, fourteen taken. It ended with one part 0.07% past its limit and all the fitting answers together inside (0.9933). The matrix it stood at, never written, differs from the original by 4.11% of the matrix. The pull of the matrix before it (layer 9's attention, 0.00007 of its tube loss) was then halved back twelve times, each read through the engine; at none did this matrix's merge come back inside, and layer 9's attention stands in the left model as it was written. The sweep ended as declared: not accepted, not finished. The replay, the own answers and the verdict have no finished model to read and were not run.

failures_only: The sweep ended at its twentieth of 70 matrices, not accepted. There is no finished model, so the replay, the own answers and the verdict were not run.

The bringing back at layer 9's feed-forward ended with one part outside after 19 rounds, 14 taken, with the ridge at its floor: size_mean, wrong group, place 160 (a move is asked there), the layer's last merge, third 1, at 1.000694 of a limit of 1.59e-6. The solver's claim that the stepped ridge brings back what arrives outside is weakened as the declaration said it would be: this bringing back and layer 8's feed-forward's both used their rounds down to the smallest ridge, and this one did not end inside.

From layer 8 on a bringing back changed 1.04%, 8.87%, 3.77% and (unwritten) 4.11% of a matrix, against 0.14% to 0.61% before. The split's premise is weakened in the part the declaration named: the groups' means themselves arrive several times past their limits at every matrix (up to 30.8 times at a matrix's own merge and 33.6 at a layer's last), and from layer 8 they need a few percent of a matrix to come back.

Nine of the eighteen matrices after the first kept under 0.0001 of the tube loss beyond their bringing back (positions 4 to 7, 11, 15 to 18). Fifteen paths ended on the read third's bounds, three with no step taken at all.

Six bringing backs had rounds of which no part was taken (positions 2, 9, 12, 16, 17 and 18: 2, 3, 1, 1, 1 and 1 rounds). The declaration's revision reported every step taken whole on the kept rows it was read on.

The machine stopped without a shutdown at 7:36:58 PM CT with both cards loaded. Position 18 was cut off and made again from the record; nothing on record was lost. A matrix written before a restart can no longer be taken back; that did not bear on the end, because the matrix taken back at position 19 was written after the restart.
The build's passes waited 1,860 s for card 0 at positions 1, 3, 5, 7 and 8 while other sessions' jobs held it.
what_this_changes: This run does not test the hypothesis: it has no finished model, and by its own declaration a sweep that ends early says the configuration is not there yet. It is this configuration's result at layer 9's feed-forward. The earlier repairs and their transfer stand as recorded.

The split, which Marcos approved on November 11, does what it was tested for at the first sixteen matrices: with the rows held to their own scale a bringing back changes 0.14% to 0.61% of a matrix where it changed 2.1% to 6.8%, the engine's own output stays inside every bound at every merge read, and ten matrices pull, to 0.62 of the tube loss at layer 6's feed-forward. What it leaves open is the means: every pull upstream moves the groups' means at the merges downstream, each matrix after has to bring them back, and at layers 8 and 9 that takes 1% to 9% of a matrix. The limits on the means and what they are counted from are Astra's to weigh; nothing here changes a bound.

The solver, which is this session's. (1) The bringing back at layers 8 and 9: read on rows kept from the left model at layer 9's feed-forward whether the same solve ends inside on another run, and which earlier matrices' changes put the 20 to 31 size means outside there. (2) The pull: fifteen of eighteen paths end on the third that is only read. A pull that holds all three thirds' bounds in its step went past that end at the one matrix it was read on in development (records/development/2026-11-10-controlled-training/README.md, position8-joint-*). It changes a declared part of step 5, so it is Marcos's to approve: Astra put it to him on November 11 (records/retrospectives/2026-11-11-all-fitting-constraints-method-check-astra.md) and no answer is on record. (3) The three paths that took no step are a separate case: whether the steps refused there fail a bound, fail to lower the tube loss, or both, is to be read on kept rows. (4) A ladder whose every ridge ends on the same read part (positions 3 to 7 and 11, weight-research-perfomance's reading) spends its time without telling more; a stop for it belongs in the next declaration.

The machine: this stop came with both cards loaded; the stop of November 10 at 8:28 PM CT did not (card 1 idle at 2% and 28 W, card 0 stepping between 44 W and 364 to 382 W: hostshield's telemetry, weight-research-perfomance's reading in records/development/2026-11-10-speed-review/README.md). What the two share is card 0's load stepping by hundreds of watts; no cause is shown. Until Marcos says otherwise this work loads one card at a time.

The bringing back that ended this sweep, run again five times on card 0 with the build's solver, ends inside every bound five times of five: 12, 16, 13, 15 and 20 rounds, 4.11% to 4.16% of the matrix changed. The build's own is the one of six that ended outside.

The end was one round: at the smallest ridge a round of which no part left less outside ended the solve. Of 59 rounds played at that ridge from two states kept late in a solve, one was such a round; its whole step, 0.05% of the matrix, brought the one part outside back in and put two others 0.04% and 0.0006% past their limits. From the state kept there, of eighteen replays the first round took no part in six; ending there, three of four solves end outside; with the round made again with the margins it has just grown, fourteen of fourteen end inside in one to four rounds. The solver makes the round again from the commit that records this. It does not reach a state where the least step is too small for the file to hold, which only a solve begun again from the matrix it stood on produced (card 1: no part taken in 13 rounds of 15, then in 26 of 26 at the smallest ridge, twice).

The first step of that bringing back (3.72% of the matrix, from 482.3 outside) answers to the reading of each third beside all the answers together, not to one family of bounds: with a family or both means not held in the script's memory it is 2.56% to 3.72%; with all the fitting answers together brought back alone, 0.83%. One state and one round: the changed search's outcome, not a decomposition of the cost and not a reading of whether the thirds' limits are needed. Astra keeps the approved readings and bounds (records/retrospectives/2026-11-11-thirds-pool-and-mean-estimators-astra.md).

That first step is not the least step at the ten passes a round has: 3.72% at pass 10, 3.16% at 20, 3.00% at 40, 2.89% at 80 and still falling; with the linear solves resolved (160 iterations a pass) 3.54%, 3.09%, 2.98%, 2.90%. The splitting is what is slow. Neither figure is a minimum certificate (Astra).

With the wrong group's mean-size limit set, in the script's memory, to the two full groups' squared difference at the asked places where the sizes differ, the bringing back changes 4.05% of the matrix in 16 rounds: holding the size where it stood is not what this bringing back costs.
